intent: Explore rotating phase-sector frames, including frames related to stroke direction, in a later rendering version.
definition: W_alpha(s,a)=exp(-i*alpha)*(zeta(s)-a); classify arg W_alpha modulo2*pi into four half-open sectors when W_alpha is finite and nonzero.
fixedFrame: A constant alpha rotates the quadrant boundaries in the output plane.
movingFrame: For a parameterized stroke s(u), define an explicit real frame angle alpha(u). If input tangent angle is chosen, state the input/output coordinate identification. Alternatively use output tangent arg(zeta prime(s(u))*s prime(u)) wherever that tangent is nonzero. Undefined tangents need an explicit invalid or fallback-frame state.
invariant: Multiplication by exp(-i*alpha) is nonzero, so W_alpha=0 iff zeta(s)=a for every defined real alpha. Phase is still undefined at a root.
controls: Compare fixed and moving frames on identical samples and targets.
Retain rotation, sampling resolution, numerical precision, draw order and blending mode separately.
Compare forward and reverse draw order when overlapping strokes are rendered.
Avoid interpreting frame-induced color boundaries as new zeros or proof of RH.
scope: Rendering and local geometric exploration; not a new theorem or an implemented next-prime algorithm.
